explanation: Future-work item from openalex:W4399803256 (2024) is unaddressed by any later corpus paper through 2026 (2 yrs). 18 later topically-near papers exist and none addresses it (two-stage matcher). Item: "Developing uncertainty estimation methods for language models that explicitly separate aleatoric uncertainty from epistemic uncertainty.". CORPUS-RELATIVE CAVEAT: 'orphaned' means unaddressed WITHIN this 113-paper corpus, not the field; the two-stage matcher's precision is limited (P≈0.64) and the corpus is a sample, so this is a weak, corpus-relative signal — not evidence the field ignored it.

consumer.kind_short: A question a paper said needed studying, that nothing else in this library followed up on
consumer.kind_long: When researchers finish a paper they usually name the questions they could not get to. We collected those, then checked whether any later paper in this library actually went and did the work. These are the ones where nothing did.
consumer.strength_meaning: There is real evidence behind this, but it rests on a small number of papers — read them before trusting it.
consumer.why: A paper said this needed studying. That was 2 years ago. Since then 18 later papers in this library worked on closely related topics, and none of them took this up.

caveats.label: Only checked within these 113 papers
caveats.text: Nothing in this library followed this up — but this library is 113 papers, not the whole field. Somebody outside it may well have answered this already. Check before you invest.
